name: montage
desc: Toolkit for assembling FITS images into custom mosaics
why: Real astronomy mosaicking software from Caltech, a genuine science tool, though its appeal depends on whether you work with FITS images.

brief.what_it_is: Montage is a toolkit for assembling FITS (Flexible Image Transport System) astronomy images into custom mosaics. You give it input FITS images and specify the target coordinates, projection, spatial sampling, rotation and background matching, and it reprojects, background-matches and co-adds them into a FITS mosaic. It also includes tools for reading and tabulating image metadata, examining images, and visualizing results with three-colour displays and catalogue overlays. The tools are ANSI-C stand-alone executables with names beginning in m (such as mAdd), also available as a library, and since version 6 as a Python package called MontagePy.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as an accurate, open-source way to build custom sky mosaics from FITS images while preserving spatial and calibration fidelity, and as a tool that runs from a desktop up to clusters and computational grids.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage describes separate engines for analysing the geometry of images on the sky, re-projecting images, rectifying background emission to a common level, and co-adding images. The 7.0 README adds HiPS tooling that builds large mosaics with the existing reprojection, background matching and co-addition modules, using a HPX projection, then repeatedly shrinks by factors of two to form a tile hierarchy and cuts 512x512 tiles.

commands_seen.context: Installs the Python binary-extension version of Montage from PyPI, offered as an alternative to building from source.
The README says the distribution contains all libraries needed to build the toolkit from a single simple make command; it bundles CFITSIO and the WCS library.

brief.install_notes: Building from source needs only a C toolchain and make, since CFITSIO and the WCS library are bundled. For Python, MontagePy needs Python 3.x (3.6+ recommended) and is distributed as binary wheels for Linux and Mac via PyPI. Native Windows executables are cross-compiled, and Cygwin is listed as a Windows option. No accounts or service sign-up are mentioned. The Homebrew caveat points to a licence download page that the user should read before use.
brief.standout: Montage has a long academic pedigree, is written in portable C, and is used as an example application in workflow and cloud research. Version 7.0 adds tools for building HiPS tile sets on a single desktop at arcminute scale, with cloud job generation for arcsecond scale. The Python wheels are built from the C code through Cython, so the same algorithms run at compiled speed.
brief.status: Maintained, with some evidence of recent activity. The homepage was rebuilt on a new VM in April 2022 and still has active news. The on-demand mosaic web service was decommissioned in March 2021 and replaced by Python notebooks. The latest versioned release dated on the homepage is 6.0 from November 2018. The GitHub README describes Montage 7.0 and has a Jenkins build badge, though it also says regression testing is only partly in place. I could not find a last-commit or 7.0 release date, so that remains unknown.
brief.caveats: Licence conflict: the Homebrew caveat says Montage is under the Caltech/JPL non-exclusive, non-commercial software licence, but the homepage and GitHub README both say it is BSD 3-clause. Check the download page before any commercial use. The on-demand web mosaic service is decommissioned, so users must run the software or notebooks themselves. The README says regression testing is only partly in place. MontagePy requires Python 3.x, and the README calls the wheel builds a moving target. The homepage's news includes a 2015 note about patching the software on Mac, which I could not check for current relevance. The homepage warns that the 2022 OS move may have subtle effects.
quotes: Montage is a toolkit for assembling Flexible Image Transport System (FITS) images into custom mosaics.

Montage is an Open Source toolkit, distributed with a BSD 3-clause license, for assembling Flexible Image Transport System (FITS) images into mosaics according to the user's custom specifications of coordinates, projection, spatial sampling, rotation and background matching.
Montage is written in ANSI-C and is portable across all common Unix-like platforms, including Linux, Solaris, Mac OSX and Cygwin on Windows.

judge.reason: A specialized astronomy toolkit that reprojects and background-matches FITS images into scientifically faithful sky mosaics is an intriguing, hands-on scientific rabbit hole.

entry.title: Montage
entry.tldr: Caltech's astronomy toolkit that reprojects, background-matches and stitches FITS sky images into custom mosaics, as about seventy small command-line programs.
entry.deeper_look:
Montage takes a pile of FITS images, the standard file format for astronomical data, and builds a single mosaic to your specification. You choose the sky coordinates, projection, spatial sampling and rotation. It reprojects each input, rectifies background emission to a common level, and co-adds the results into a new FITS image. The aim, in the README's framing, is an accurate open-source way to do this while preserving spatial and calibration fidelity.

The design is the interesting part. The homepage describes separate engines for analysing image geometry on the sky, re-projecting, background rectification and co-addition. Each engine is a stand-alone ANSI-C executable whose name starts with m, such as mAdd or mProject, and the `*Exec` variants run a step over a whole directory of images. A mosaic is a pipeline you assemble from these parts, which is also why Montage turns up as an example application in workflow and cloud research. The same code runs on a desktop, a cluster or a grid.

There are also tools for reading and tabulating image metadata, examining images, and visualizing results with three-colour displays and catalogue overlays. Since version 6 the algorithms are available from Python as MontagePy, built from the C code through Cython. The 7.0 README adds HiPS tooling: it builds a large mosaic in a HPX projection, shrinks it repeatedly by factors of two to form a tile hierarchy, and cuts 512x512 tiles.

The door it opens is how sky images get stitched together at all. Pixels from different telescopes sit on different grids, projections and background levels, and the problem is making them agree.
entry.install:
brew install montage
# Homebrew prints a licence caveat pointing to http://montage.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/download.html. Read it before use.
# Alternative: pip install MontagePy (Python 3.x, binary wheels for Linux and Mac)
# You will need your own FITS images to get a mosaic out of it.

Shows usage for the reprojection step that resamples an image onto a new coordinate grid.

entry.whats_unique: It is a long-standing academic mosaicking toolkit written in portable C, split into small single-purpose programs that scale from a laptop to computational grids. The same algorithms are also available from Python.
entry.caveats: The Homebrew caveat says a Caltech/JPL non-commercial licence applies while the homepage and README say BSD 3-clause, so check the download page before commercial use; the on-demand web service has been decommissioned, and the README says regression testing is only partly in place.
